rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative “that” points to the ruling just discussed.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى الحكم المذكور عندنا

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: For residents of the Sacred Mosque there is no tamattuʿ or qirān; if one performs tamattuʿ, he owes a compensatory sacrificial animal.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا متعة ولا قران لحاضري المسجد الحرام عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A resident of the Sacred Mosque is someone living within the distance of a shortened journey from the sanctuary; those closer are residents or legally equivalent.
rows.anchor: من كان من الحرم على مسافة القصر عندنا

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: He defines residents as those whose homes are beyond the miqat.
rows.anchor: ومن مسكنه وراء الميقات عنده

rows.speaker: طاوس
rows.claim: He defines the relevant residents as the people of the ḥill.
rows.anchor: وأهل الحل عند طاوس

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: He defines them as people who are not Meccans.
rows.anchor: وغير المكي عند مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands observance of His commands and prohibitions, especially during pilgrimage.
rows.anchor: في المحافظة على أوامره ونواهيه وخصوصا في الحج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge that God is severe in punishment should restrain the unobservant from disobedience.
rows.anchor: لمن لم يتقه كي يصدكم للعلم به عن العصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The months of pilgrimage means the time for performing Hajj.
rows.anchor: أي وقته. كقولك البرد شهران.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author counts Shawwal, Dhu al-Qadah, and nine days of Dhu al-Hijjah through the night of sacrifice; Abu Hanifa counts ten days, and Malik the whole month.
rows.anchor: وهي: شوال وذو القعدة وتسعة من ذي الحجة بليلة النحر عندنا

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: He counts the first ten days of Dhu al-Hijjah among the Hajj months.
rows.anchor: والعشر عند أبي حنيفة رحمه الله تعالى

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: He counts all of Dhu al-Hijjah as part of the Hajj months.
rows.anchor: وذي الحجة كله عند مالك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disagreement turns on whether the months delimit entry into ihram, the performance of rites, or the period in which no other rites are appropriate.
rows.anchor: وبناء على الخلاف على أن المراد بوقته

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Because of his understanding of the Hajj period, Malik disliked performing ʿumrah during the remainder of Dhu al-Hijjah.
rows.anchor: فإن مالكا كره العمرة في بقية ذي الحجة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Although ihram before Shawwal is valid, Abu Hanifa regarded it as disapproved.
rows.anchor: وإن صح الإحرام به قبل شوال فقد استكرهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural months can denote a part standing for the whole, or a plural used for anything greater than one.
rows.anchor: إقامة للبعض مقام الكل، أو إطلاقا للجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person imposes Hajj on himself by entering ihram; Abu Hanifa says it is imposed by the talbiyah or by bringing a sacrificial animal.
rows.anchor: بالإحرام فيهن عندنا، أو بالتلبية أو سوق الهدي عند أبي حنيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This supports al-Shafiʿi’s view that whoever enters ihram for Hajj must complete it.
rows.anchor: وهو دليل على ما ذهب إليه الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى وأن من أحرم بالحج لزمه الإتمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafath means intercourse, or obscene speech.
rows.anchor: فلا جماع، أو فلا فحش من الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fusuq means departing from the bounds of sacred law through sins and committing forbidden acts.
rows.anchor: ولا خروج عن حدود الشرع بالسيئات وارتكاب المحظورات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jidal means disputing with servants and travel companions.
rows.anchor: ولا مراء مع الخدم والرفقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three negations function as emphatic prohibitions; conduct already objectionable becomes worse during Hajj, like wearing silk in prayer.
rows.anchor: نفي الثلاثة على قصد النهي للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ornamented, melodic recitation of the Qurʾan departs from ordinary impulse and habit toward pure worship.
rows.anchor: والتطريب بقراءة القرآن لأنه خروج عن مقتضى الطبع والعادة

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read the first two prohibitions in the nominative as saying that neither rafath nor fusuq should occur, and the third in the accusative as declaring that dispute is absent.
rows.anchor: والأولين بالرفع على معنى: لا يكونن رفث ولا فسوق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh had agreements with other Arabs and stopped at al-Mashʿar al-Haram; the dispute ended when they were ordered to stop at ʿArafat too.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن قريشا كانت تحالف سائر العرب فتقف بالمشعر الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mention of God’s knowledge of good deeds encourages good immediately after the prohibition of evil, so good can replace evil.
rows.anchor: حث على الخير عقب به النهي عن الشر ليستدل به ويستعمل مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pilgrims should provision themselves with taqwa for the Hereafter, the best provision.
rows.anchor: وتزودوا لمعادكم التقوى فإنه خير زاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is said the verse was revealed about Yemenis who made pilgrimage without provisions, claiming trust in God and becoming a burden on others; they were told to provision themselves and avoid burdening people with requests.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أهل اليمن كانوا يحجون ولا يتزودون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Laghw is disregarded speech and an oath without a deliberate commitment, such as a slip of the tongue or saying “no, by God” merely for emphasis without understanding its meaning.
rows.anchor: ولغو اليمين مالا عقد معه كما سبق به اللسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God imposes neither punishment nor expiation for an oath without intent, but does one or both for intended oaths in which the heart agrees with the tongue.
rows.anchor: لا يؤاخذكم الله بعقوبة ولا كفارة بما لا قصد معه

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa defines laghw as swearing on the basis of a mistaken belief; there is no punishment for an erroneous oath, but there is for a deliberate lie.
rows.anchor: أن يحلف الرجل بناء على ظنه الكاذب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forgiving because He does not hold people accountable for laghw oaths.
rows.anchor: والله غفور } حيث لم يؤاخذ باللغو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forbearing because He delays accountability for a serious oath to allow repentance.
rows.anchor: حليم } حيث لم يعجل بالمؤاخذة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Be informed of war” means that the usurers should know that God and His Messenger are at war with them.
rows.anchor: من أذن بالشيء إذا علم به

rows.speaker: حمزة وعاصم
rows.claim: They read “then inform others of it,” deriving the verb from listening, one of the routes to knowledge.
rows.anchor: من الأذن وهو الاستماع فإنه من طرق العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite “war” magnifies the threat; it entails fighting an unrepentant usurer until he returns to God’s command, like a rebel, but does not entail unbelief.
rows.anchor: وتنكير حرب للتعظيم وذلك يقتضي أن يقاتل المربي بعد الاستتابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the verse was revealed, Thaqif said they could not wage war against God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: أنها لما نزلت قالت ثقيف لا يدي لنا بحرب الله ورسوله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Upon repentance from usury, creditors may claim only their principal: taking more wrongs debtors, while delaying or reducing repayment wrongs creditors.
rows.anchor: { فلكم رءوس أمولكم لا تظلمون } بأخذ الزيادة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By implication, a person who refuses repentance forfeits even the principal, since persisting in declaring usury lawful is apostasy and his property becomes spoils.
rows.anchor: إذ المصر على التحليل مرتد وماله فيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can mean that a debtor has fallen into hardship; an alternate reading makes the debtor “one who has hardship.”
rows.anchor: وإن وقع غريم ذو عسرة. وقرىء «ذا عسرة»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Then deferment” can be a ruling, an obligation upon creditors, or a command that it be a deferment.
rows.anchor: فالحكم نظرة، أو فعليكم نظرة، أو فليكن نظرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading can say that the creditor is waiting for payment or is the one granting respite; another is an imperative to grant respite.
rows.anchor: أي فالمستحق ناظره بمعنى منتظره، أو صاحب نظرته على طريق النسب

rows.speaker: نافع وحمزة
rows.claim: They read maysarah with a damma on the sīn; both vocalizations are Arabic variants.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحمزة بضم السين، وهما لغتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both forms are also read in annexation with the tāʾ omitted, as in the cited wording from 9:77.
rows.anchor: بحذف التاء عند الإضافة كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving charity means writing off the debt; ʿAsim reads the ṣād with a light pronunciation.
rows.anchor: { وأن تصدقوا } بالإبراء. وقرأ عاصم بتخفيف الصاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiving the debt is more rewarded than granting time, or better than the amount received because its reward is multiplied and lasting.
rows.anchor: أكثر ثوابا من الإنظار، أو خير مما تأخذون لمضاعفة ثوابه ودوامه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The source cites a Prophetic report that a Muslim creditor who postpones a due debt receives charity for every day of delay.
rows.anchor: لا يحل دين رجل مسلم فيؤخره إلا كان له بكل يوم صدقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “If you know” refers to what this charitable conduct contains: a fine and abundant remembrance.
rows.anchor: ما فيه من الذكر الجميل الجزيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The day to fear is the Day of Resurrection, or the day of death; people should prepare for their return to God.
rows.anchor: يوم القيامة، أو يوم الموت فتأهبوا لمصيركم إليه.

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read the verb with an open tāʾ and a kasra on the jīm.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب بفتح التاء وكسر الجيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each soul is repaid for what it did, whether good or evil.
rows.anchor: جزاء ما عملت من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No one is wronged by a reduction in reward or an increase in punishment.
rows.anchor: بنقص ثواب وتضعيف عقاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that this was the last verse brought by Gabriel, who told the Prophet to place it at the head of verse 280 of al-Baqara; the Prophet lived another 21 days, though other reports give 81 days, seven days, or three hours.
rows.anchor: أنها آخر آية نزل بها جبريل عليه السلام وقال ضعها في رأس المائتين والثمانين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing in the world is hidden from God, whether universal or particular, faith or unbelief; “heaven and earth” mark the limits of human perception.
rows.anchor: أي شيء كائن في العالم كليا كان أو جزئيا، إيمانا أو كفرا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth comes first as a progression from lower to higher, and because the intended subject is what people commit on earth.
rows.anchor: وإنما قدم الأرض ترقيا من الأدنى إلى الأعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s complete knowledge serves as evidence that He is living.
rows.anchor: وهو كالدليل على كونه حيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s shaping people in the womb as He wills is evidence of His sustaining power; the perfected creation of the fetus demonstrates His knowledge.
rows.anchor: كالدليل على القيومية، والاستدلال على أنه عالم بإتقان فعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading says God formed people for Himself and for His worship.
rows.anchor: أي صوركم لنفسه وعبادته.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no deity but God, because no one else knows all that He knows or can do what He does.
rows.anchor: إذ لا يعلم غيره جملة ما يعلمه ولا يقدر على مثل ما يفعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names the Mighty and the Wise indicate perfect power and consummate wisdom.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى كمال قدرته وتناهي حكمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage is said to argue against those who claim Jesus is a lord; the Najran delegation disputed with the Prophet, and the opening eighty-plus verses were revealed to establish the case and answer their doubts.
rows.anchor: هذا حجاج على من زعم أن عيسى كان ربا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Allāhumma, the mīm replaces the vocative yāʾ, so they cannot be combined; this name also has unusual forms with yāʾ, the definite article, a hamza, and oath tāʾ.
rows.anchor: الميم عوض عن يا ولذلك لا يجتمعان، وهو من خصائص هذا الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative derivation is yā Allāh, ummanā bi-khayr, shortened by dropping the vocative, verb complements, and hamza.
rows.anchor: أصله يا الله أمنا بخير، فخفف بحذف حرف النداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Master of dominion means disposing of what can be disposed of as owners dispose of their property; Sibawayh treats it as a second vocative because the mīm prevents an adjectival reading.
rows.anchor: يتصرف فيما يمكن التصرف فيه تصرف الملاك فيما يملكون

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh regards “Master of dominion” as a second vocative, since the mīm prevents it from being an adjective.
rows.anchor: وهو نداء ثان عند سيبويه فإن الميم عنده تمنع الوصفية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first mention of dominion is general, while giving and taking dominion refer to parts of it.
rows.anchor: فالملك الأول عام والآخران بعضان منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also said that dominion means prophethood, transferred by God from one people to another.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد بالملك النبوة ونزعها نقلها من قوم إلى قوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Honor and abasement may occur in this world, the next, or both, through victory or reversal and success or abandonment.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا أو في الآخرة، أو فيهما بالنصر والإدبار والتوفيق والخذلان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only good is named because it is intended in itself while particular evil is incidental to a greater good; propriety in address is another explanation.
rows.anchor: ذكر الخير وحده لأنه المقضي بالذات، والشر مقضي بالعرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the verse followed the trench episode: the Prophet struck an immense rock three times, with flashes revealing the palaces of al-Hira, Rome, and Sanʿa; Gabriel promised the community would prevail, while hypocrites mocked the prediction.
rows.anchor: فجاء عليه الصلاة والسلام فأخذ المعول منه فضربها ضربة صدعتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The close, “You are capable of everything,” makes clear that evil too is in God’s power.
rows.anchor: فنبه على أن الشر أيضا بيده بقوله { إنك على كل شيء قدير }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address “People of the Book” includes both scriptural communities; it is also said to mean the Najran delegation or the Jews of Medina.
rows.anchor: يعم أهل الكتابين. وقيل يريد به وفد نجران، أو يهود المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shared word is a principle on which messengers and scriptures agree, and the following clauses explain it.
rows.anchor: لا يختلف فيها الرسل والكتب ويفسرها ما بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship God alone means affirming His unity in worship and devoting worship sincerely to Him.
rows.anchor: أن نوحده بالعبادة ونخلص فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Associating nothing with God means neither making anything His partner in deserving worship nor regarding anything else as worthy of worship.
rows.anchor: ولا نجعل غيره شريكا له في استحقاق العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking one another as lords includes calling Ezra or the Messiah God’s son and obeying religious scholars in innovations about what is lawful or forbidden, although they are fellow humans.
rows.anchor: ولا نطيع الأحبار فيما أحدثوا من التحريم والتحليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source links the discussion to 9:31; ʿAdi ibn Hatim said they did not worship their clergy, and the Prophet replied that following their rulings on lawful and forbidden was precisely that.
rows.anchor: قال عدي بن حاتم: ما كنا نعبدهم يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they turn away from monotheism, the Muslims should say that the evidence has bound them and they must acknowledge the Muslims’ submission.
rows.anchor: فإن تولوا } عن التوحيد. { فقولوا اشهدوا بأنا مسلمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that the People of the Book should acknowledge that the Muslims are Muslim while they are not.
rows.anchor: فاعترفوا بأنا مسلمون دونكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they should admit they reject what the scriptures state and the messengers affirm.
rows.anchor: أو اعترفوا بأنكم كافرون بما نطقت به الكتب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The argument proceeds gradually: it explains how Jesus’ life stages contradict divinity, answers doubts, invites them to mutual imprecation, then returns to an easier appeal based on Jesus, the Gospel, the prophets, and scriptures; when even that fails, it calls for public acknowledgment of Muslim faith.
rows.anchor: من المبالغة في الإرشاد وحسن التدرج في الحجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse denies and rebuts the claim that Jesus is a deity to be worshipped.
rows.anchor: تكذيب ورد على عبده عيسى عليه السلام.

rows.speaker: أبو رافع القرظي والسيد النجراني
rows.claim: They asked Muhammad whether he wanted them to worship him and take him as lord; he denied that he was sent to command worship of anyone but God, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: أن أبا رافع القرظي والسيد النجراني قالا: يا محمد أتريد أن نعبدك

rows.speaker: رجل
rows.claim: A man asked whether they should greet the Prophet as one another did and prostrate to him; he said no one should prostrate except God, but they should honor their Prophet and recognize rightful claims.
rows.anchor: قال رجل يا رسول الله نسلم عليك كما يسلم بعضنا على بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rabbānī is ascribed to the Lord with an added alif and nūn, like liḥyānī and raqibānī, and is complete in knowledge and action.
rows.anchor: والرباني منسوب إلى الرب بزيادة الألف والنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means that they became teachers of scripture and studied it; the purpose of teaching and learning is to know truth and good for belief and action.
rows.anchor: بسبب كونكم معلمين الكتاب وبسبب كونكم دارسين له

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read taʿlamūn as meaning “being knowledgeable.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب تعلمون بمعنى عالمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms of tadrusūn may derive from teaching or from adrasa, meaning to study; the common reading can also mean teaching scripture to people.
rows.anchor: من التدريس وتدرسون من أدرس بمعنى درس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kaʾayyin comes from ayy with kāf prefixed, means “how many,” and ends in a tanwīn written unusually.
rows.anchor: أصله أي دخلت الكاف عليها وصارت بمعنى كم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: He reads kāʾin; the explanation involves metathesis, then deleting one yāʾ for ease and changing the other to alif, as in Ṭāʾī.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير «وكائن» ككاعن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A prophet” explains the preceding expression.
rows.anchor: من نبي } بيان له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribbiyyūn may mean learned, pious rabbāniyyūn, worshippers of their Lord, or groups; the last derives the term from ribba, a group, for emphasis.
rows.anchor: ربانيون علماء أتقياء، أو عابدون لربهم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read qutila, “was killed”; it may refer to the ribbiyyūn or to the Prophet, with the ribbiyyūn then construed as circumstantial, and a geminated reading supports the first analysis.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو ويعقوب «قتل»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ribbiyyūn is also read with fatḥa on the rāʾ, reflecting the original form, or with ḍamma, a change in the relational ending like kasra.
rows.anchor: { ربيون } بالفتح على الأصل وبالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not flag or lose resolve over what befell them in God’s path, whether the Prophet or some of them were killed.
rows.anchor: فما فتروا ولم ينكسر جدهم لما أصابهم من قتل النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They did not weaken against the enemy or in their religion, and did not submit to the enemy.
rows.anchor: وما ضعفوا } عن العدو أو في الدين. { وما استكانوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istakānū derives either from stillness, as the submissive stills himself for another to act upon, or from being, as he seeks to become subject to the one he obeys; this describes their response to rumors of the Prophet’s death.
rows.anchor: وهذا تعريف بما أصابهم عند الإرجاف بقتله عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God loves the patient, granting them victory and raising their standing.
rows.anchor: فينصرهم ويعظم قدرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “When God took” means “remember the time when He took.”
rows.anchor: أي اذكر وقت أخذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those given the Scripture here are its scholars.
rows.anchor: يريد به العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pledge to explain Scripture and not conceal it recounts God’s address to them; the pronoun refers to the Book.
rows.anchor: واللام جواب القسم الذي ناب عنه قوله: { أخذ الله ميثق الذين } والضمير للكتاب.

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم
rows.claim: They read the pledge verbs in the third person because the scholars are absent from direct address.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وعاصم في رواية ابن عياش بالياء لأنهم غيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām answers an oath implied by the statement that God took their covenant.
rows.anchor: واللام جواب القسم الذي ناب عنه قوله: { أخذ الله ميثق الذين }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cast aside the covenant, meaning they disregarded it; this image contrasts with keeping it before their eyes.
rows.anchor: فلم يراعوه ولم يتلفتوا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They exchanged the covenant for the trifles and passing goods of this world, a wretched bargain.
rows.anchor: وأخذوا بدله. { ثمنا قليلا } من حطام الدنيا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report warns that whoever conceals knowledge from those entitled to it will be bridled with fire.
rows.anchor: من كتم علما عن أهله ألجم بلجام من نار

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says God took a covenant from scholars to teach before taking a covenant from the ignorant to learn.
rows.anchor: ما أخذ الله على أهل الجهل أن يتعلموا حتى أخذ على أهل العلم أن يعلموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to the Prophet; reading the bāʾ with ḍamma extends it to the Prophet and believers.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم، ومن ضم الباء جعل الخطاب له وللمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse warns against thinking that people who rejoice in deception and concealing truth, and seek praise for keeping the covenant and revealing truth when they did not, are safe from punishment.
rows.anchor: بما فعلوا من التدليس وكتمان الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is for their unbelief and deception.
rows.anchor: بكفرهم وتدليسهم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read the two occurrences with yāʾ and different vowels on the bāʾ; the people rejoicing become the subject, with the objects supplied from the emphatic clause.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو بالياء وفتح الباء في الأول وضمها في الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One occasion report says Jews were asked about something in the Torah, answered contrary to its contents, pretended they had told the truth, and rejoiced in their deed.
rows.anchor: سأل اليهود عن شيء مما في التوراة فأخبروه بخلاف ما كان فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says it was revealed about people who stayed behind from a military expedition, then claimed their decision had been prudent and sought praise for it.
rows.anchor: نزلت في قوم تخلفوا عن الغزو ثم اعتذروا بأنهم رأوا المصلحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further view says it concerns hypocrites who rejoiced in hypocrisy and sought Muslims’ praise for a faith they did not truly practice.
rows.anchor: وقيل: نزلت في المنافقين فإنهم يفرحون بمنافقتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “People” is an address encompassing all the children of Adam.
rows.anchor: خطاب يعم بني آدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one soul from which humanity was created is Adam.
rows.anchor: من نفس وحدة } هي آدم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His spouse was created from him: Eve was made from one of Adam’s ribs.
rows.anchor: وخلق منه أمكم حواء من ضلع من أضلاعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, an omitted clause means “from one soul He created, and from it He created its spouse,” reaffirming humanity’s single origin.
rows.anchor: أو محذوف تقديره من نفس واحدة خلقها وخلق منها زوجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spreading of many men and women explains how they descend from the original pair; the verse mentions many men without repeating “many” for women because wisdom requires women to be more numerous.
rows.anchor: ونشر من تلك النفس والزوج المخلوقة منها بنين وبنات كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The masculine plural “many” follows the collective construction.
rows.anchor: وذكر { كثيرا } حملا على الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The origin story grounds the command to fear God in His overwhelming power and abundant blessing, which call for fear and obedience.
rows.anchor: لما فيها من الدلالة على القدرة القاهرة التي من حقها أن تخشى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the command prepares people for piety in the rights of household members and fellow human beings discussed in the following verses.
rows.anchor: تمهيد الأمر بالتقوى فيما يتصل بحقوق أهل منزله وبني جنسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading has khāliqun and bāththun with an omitted subject, estimated as “and He is creator and spreader.”
rows.anchor: وقرىء «وخالق» «وباث» على حذف مبتدأ تقديره وهو خالق وباث.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasaʾalūn derives from tata-sāʾalūn, with the second tāʾ assimilated into the sīn.
rows.anchor: وأصله تتساءلون فأدغمت التاء الثانية في السين

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They omit one of the two tāʾs in the verb.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وحمزة والكسائي بطرحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-arḥām can be accusative by coordination with the understood object of the preposition, or with God as the object of “fear”: fear God and maintain kinship.
rows.anchor: والأرحام } بالنصب عطف على محل الجار والمجرور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author interprets the second accusative construction as commanding people to maintain kinship and not sever it.
rows.anchor: أي اتقوا الله واتقوا الأرحام فصلوها ولا تقطعوها

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza reads al-arḥām in the genitive, coordinated with the pronoun after the preposition; the construction is weak because it is like a part of a word.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة بالجر عطفا على الضمير المجرور وهو ضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A nominative reading treats al-arḥām as a subject with an omitted predicate: it too is something to be guarded or invoked by.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالرفع على أنه مبتدأ محذوف الخبر تقديره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By pairing kinship with His honored name, God indicates that maintaining family ties is owed for His sake.
rows.anchor: إذ قرن الأرحام باسمه الكريم على أن صلتها بمكان منه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Prophetic report depicts kinship as suspended from the Throne, asking God to join whoever maintains it and sever whoever cuts it.
rows.anchor: الرحم معلقة بالعرش تقول ألا من وصلني وصله الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is a guardian over people, preserving and observing them.
rows.anchor: حافظا مطلعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition means not to marry the women whom one’s fathers married; mā is used instead of man because it describes them.
rows.anchor: ولا تنكحوا التي نكحها آباؤكم، وإنما ذكر ما دون من لأنه أريد به الصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, mā is a verbal noun, with the object understood from the verbal expression.
rows.anchor: وقيل ما مصدرية على إرادة المفعول من المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Of women” explains what the fathers married.
rows.anchor: { من النساء } بيان ما نكح على الوجهين.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Except what is past” may except the punishment implied by the prohibition, or be an emphatic exception from the wording; it means, “do not marry your fathers’ wives, if it were possible to marry them.”
rows.anchor: استثناء من المعنى اللازم للنهي وكأنه قيل:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the exception is disconnected: past conduct is not liable to sanction because it is already over.
rows.anchor: وقيل الاستثناء منقطع ومعناه لكن ما قد سلف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is because marrying them is obscene before God and hateful to people of honor; a son by his father’s wife is called a maqtī.
rows.anchor: إن نكاحهن كان فاحشة عند الله ما رخص فيه لأمة من الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The path is evil for whoever sees and follows it.
rows.anchor: { وساء سبيلا } سبيل من يراه ويفعله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse prohibits marrying the listed women, not the women themselves; marriage is the main intended relation and the context confirms it, as “prohibited to you is carrion” means eating it.
rows.anchor: ليس المراد تحريم ذواتهن بل تحريم نكاحهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mothers include the woman who bore a person and all maternal and paternal grandmothers; daughters include daughters and all granddaughters.
rows.anchor: وأمهاتكم تعم من ولدتك أو ولدت من ولدك وإن علت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sisters include the three lines of sisterhood; likewise the other categories extend through ascending and descending generations.
rows.anchor: وأخواتكم الأخوات من الأوجه الثلاثة. وكذلك الباقيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paternal aunt is any woman descended through a male child of one’s male ancestor; the maternal aunt is through a female child of one’s female ancestor, near or distant.
rows.anchor: والعمة كل أنثى ولدها من ولد ذكرا ولدك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nieces through brothers and sisters include both close and remote descendants.
rows.anchor: وبنات الأخ وبنات الأخت تتناول القربى والبعدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives milk kinship the status of lineage, naming a wet nurse a mother and a fellow nursling a sibling; the rule follows the wet nurse and the child’s milk-producing father.
rows.anchor: نزل الله الرضاعة منزلة النسب حتى سمى المرضعة أما والمرضعة أختا

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet says that breastfeeding prohibits the same relations as lineage.
rows.anchor: يحرم من الرضاع ما يحرم من النسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects including a man’s milk-sister or milk-brother’s mother under this rule; their prohibition in blood relations arises from affinity, not milk kinship.
rows.anchor: واستثناء أخت ابن الرجل وأم أخيه من الرضاع من هذا الأصل ليس بصحيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sequence lists lineage prohibitions, then breastfeeding because it is like lineage, then affinity because its prohibition arises incidentally from marriage.
rows.anchor: ذكر أولا محرمات النسب ثم محرمات الرضاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabāʾib is the plural of rabība, a wife’s child by another man, named for usually being raised as one’s own; it is a passive form that became a noun.
rows.anchor: والربائب جمع ربيبة. والربيب ولد المرأة من آخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “of your women” attaches to stepdaughters, and the following relative clause restricts the wording and ruling by consensus.
rows.anchor: ومن نسائكم متعلق بربائبكم، واللاتي بصلتها صفة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attaching the clause to mothers would force min to mean explanation rather than origin, and one word cannot bear two meanings according to most grammarians.
rows.anchor: والكلمة الواحدة لا تحمل على معنيين عند جمهور الأدباء

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali is reported to treat “in your care” as a condition for the stepdaughter prohibition.
rows.anchor: وقد روي عن علي رضي الله تعالى عنه أنه جعله شرطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority view is that the condition is not restricted to stepdaughters actually in one’s custody.
rows.anchor: وإليه ذهب جمهور العلماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “you entered upon them” means being alone with the women under the curtain, a euphemism for intercourse.
rows.anchor: دخلتم بهن أي دخلتم معهن الستر وهي كناية عن الجماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Affinity prohibitions can also result from intercourse outside a valid marriage, including intercourse by mistake or with a slave woman.
rows.anchor: ويؤثر في حرمة المصاهرة ما ليس بزنا كالوطء بشبهة

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa treats touching one’s wife and similar contact as consummation.
rows.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة لمس المنكوحة ونحوه كالدخول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Explicitly stating the rule for a marriage without intercourse blocks an inference by analogy.
rows.anchor: تصريح بعد إشعار دفعا للقياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A son’s ḥalīla is his wife; the term derives either from being lawful to him or from living with him.
rows.anchor: سميت الزوجة حليلة لحلها أو لحلولها مع الزوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “From your loins” excludes adopted sons, but not sons’ sons.
rows.anchor: احتراز عن المتبنين لا عن أبناء الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ban on combining two sisters is coordinated grammatically with the forbidden relations and appears to cover ownership as well as marriage; Uthman and Ali cite this ban against the permission in the next verse.
rows.anchor: في موضع الرفع عطفا على المحرمات، والظاهر أن الحرمة غير مقصورة على النكاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line is cited as an exception where the relation can be understood as connectedness.
rows.anchor: على معنى أن أمهات النساء وبناتهن متصلات بهن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet distinguished the rules: after divorce before consummation, a man may marry his former wife’s daughter but not her mother; the generality of scholars follows this.
rows.anchor: " إنه لا بأس أن يتزوج ابنتها ولا يحل له أن يتزوج أمها "

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report from Ali restricts the prohibition in both cases.
rows.anchor: غير أنه روي عن علي رضي الله تعالى عنه تقييد التحريم فيهما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second relative clause cannot modify both occurrences of “women,” because their governing words differ.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون الموصول الثاني صفة للنساءين لأن عاملهما مختلف،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The custody phrase strengthens the rationale: stepdaughters resemble one’s own children when their mothers are consummated and the girls are in or near one’s care.
rows.anchor: وفائدة قوله { في حجوركم } تقوية العلة وتكميلها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mothers and stepdaughters include both near and distant generations.
rows.anchor: والأمهات والربائب يتناولان القريبة والبعيدة،
